diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride) act within the collecting 
and convoluted tubules, where they prevent sodium-potassium
exchange and reduce aldosterone stimulation.
Medications called ACE inhibitors (Captopril) competitively 
block the enzyme that converts angiotensin I into angiotensin
II. Th is results in vasodilation, a decrease in vasopressin release, 
and a resulting decrease in BP.
